title: Add audit events for image channel/version changes on fleet pools
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: - Internal: image channel/version changes for Dedicated/shared pools now emit audit events (actor, before/after, reason, request id) for compliance and incident forensics.
description:
## Context
As part of the provision-to-ready automation rollout, we are standardizing golden image channels (candidate -> stable) and pinning pool image versions. During the us-east/A100 staged rollout we had a quarantine spike and had to quickly determine who/what changed image configuration on the affected pool(s). Today those changes are visible via config history in a few places, but they are not captured as first-class audit events.

This PR emits explicit audit events whenever a pool’s image channel or pinned image version changes (including promotions and rollbacks). These events are designed to be consumable by SecOps/compliance tooling and also useful during incident response/postmortems.

## What’s included
- New audit event type: `fleet.pool.image_config_changed`
- Events emitted on:
  - `image_channel` change (e.g., `candidate` -> `stable`)
  - pinned `image_version` change (e.g., `gpuimg-2025.10.21-1` -> `gpuimg-2025.10.23-2`)
  - explicit “clear pin” operations (pin removed)
- Captured fields:
  - `pool_id`, `region`, `pool_type` (dedicated/shared)
  - `before` + `after` (channel + version)
  - `actor` (service account or user), `actor_type`
  - `reason` (freeform, required for manual changes)
  - `request_id`, `source` (api/automation), and `git_sha` of the control-plane deploy
- Emission is centralized in the pool update pathway (so we don’t miss changes from future callers)
- Guardrails:
  - No per-node identifiers in event payload
  - Size capped + reason truncated (server-side)
  - Event emission is “best effort” but failures are surfaced in metrics and logs

## Why this way
- Compliance needs an immutable record of configuration changes and the identity that performed them.
- Incident response needs to quickly answer: what changed, when, by whom, and what was the intended reason.
- We intentionally avoid logging the entire pool spec to prevent accidental leakage and keep events stable.

## Testing
- Unit tests for:
  - channel-only changes
  - version-only changes
  - channel+version changes
  - no-op updates (no event)
  - actor attribution for service-to-service calls
- Integration test with the audit sink in `dev` using a fake request id.

## Rollout / operational notes
- Event volume expected to be low (pool config changes are infrequent).
- If the audit sink is degraded, pool updates continue; we increment `audit_emit_failures_total{event_type=...}` and log at WARN with request id.
- Follow-up: wire these events into the readiness UI “change history” panel (out of scope for this PR).

Refs: ENG-4826 (image channels), ENG-4822 (readiness state machine control-plane work).
commits: control-plane: add audit event schema + constants for fleet pool events
fleet: emit audit event on pool image channel/version update (before/after + actor attribution)
security: require reason on manual pool image updates; truncate + validate
tests: unit + integration coverage for image_config_changed event emission
observability: add counters + latency histogram for audit emission path
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Nice. One request: can we ensure we emit exactly once per update request (even if both channel+version change) so downstream doesn’t have to de-dupe? Also please confirm the event is emitted after the DB transaction commits.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated to emit a single `image_config_changed` event containing both before/after values. Emission now happens post-commit (hooked into the update service return path) and includes the DB commit timestamp used as `event_time`.

Marcus Lin (security review): Please do not include raw request body or arbitrary annotations in the audit payload. Also, require a reason for human-initiated changes; automation can use a fixed reason string. Add size caps to prevent abuse.

Benji Okafor (author): Ack. Payload is now strictly `{pool_id, region, pool_type, before, after, actor, actor_type, reason, request_id, source, git_sha}`. Added `reason` validation: required if `actor_type=user`. Added truncation to 256 chars + rejects control characters.

Vanessa Ortiz (review): This will help a lot. Can we include `image_channel` values normalized (candidate/stable) and add a note about rollbacks? Also add a metric so we can alert if the sink is failing silently during a rollout window.

Benji Okafor (author): Normalization added (enum -> canonical string). Docs call out rollback flows (stable -> candidate + version pin change). Added `audit_emit_failures_total` + `audit_emit_latency_ms` and dashboard hook is tracked separately.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Can we ensure actor attribution works for service-to-service calls from the provisioning orchestrator? I’ve seen `unknown` in a few places.
Benji Okafor (author): Fixed: we now propagate `actor` via request context and default to the mTLS principal when present. Tests cover both user JWT and service principal cases.
Ethan Park (approval): LGTM. Thanks for keeping the emission post-commit and for the no-op guard.
Marcus Lin (approval): LGTM with the caps + reason requirement.
Vanessa Ortiz (approval): Approved. Please ping #eng-infra once merged so we can reference this in the rollout checklist.
